answers.answer: Select 3 randomly chosen Escape Pods for four players. Place the lowest-numbered in Section A, the next in B, then alternate A/B; all start Locked side up. The Intruder bag starts with 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, and 3 Adults plus 1 additional Adult per player (7 Adults in a four-player game).
answers.evidence: Setup steps 7 and 10; Key numbers.

answers.answer: Remove Corporate and Personal Objective cards that show a player count above the actual player count, shuffle the two decks separately, and deal each player one of each before Character draft. At the First Encounter, each player chooses one of the two Objectives and removes the rejected card face down from the game without looking at it. Eggs are not Intruders, so they do not trigger that choice; the trigger is the first Intruder miniature appearing on the board.
answers.evidence: Setup step 16; Critical gameplay moments — First Encounter.

answers.answer: Discard the used Action card and two additional Action cards to pay its printed cost of 2. The two Contamination cards cannot be discarded to pay an Action cost. If the card has two sections separated by OR, choose one section/effect.
answers.evidence: Actions — Action Cost and Actions from Action cards.

answers.answer: The Character takes 1 Light Wound after finishing their own round in the burning Room, including a round in which they take one Action and then pass. Once they pass, they cannot take further Actions that Player Phase, but may discard any number of cards when passing. Fire damage happens after each Character's own round, so later players' rounds do not cause this Character to take further Fire damage that turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Player rounds; Fire markers.

answers.answer: On entering an unexplored Room, flip the Room tile face up, reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then remove that token to the box. Set the Room tile's Item count by rotating it so the token's number faces the board's Item Counter symbol; do not set a count for the Nest or Room Covered in Slime. Resolve the Exploration effect: Silence cancels the Noise roll; Danger cancels it and moves all eligible neighboring Intruders in, or, if none are eligible, places Noise in every connected Corridor that lacks one; other listed effects place their marker (Slime, Fire, Malfunction, or Door). If ordinary Noise is called for, an empty destination gets a Noise roll, but a Room already containing a Character or Intruder does not. Silence gives no marker; Danger has the movement/all-connected-Corridors rule above. An already occupied destination causes no Noise roll.
answers.evidence: Movement, Rooms, and Corridors; Exploration tokens; Noise roll.

answers.answer: Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards. It follows normal Movement restrictions and replaces the usual Noise roll after moving with placing a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination Room. It is forbidden in Combat and if all Corridors connected to the destination already have Noise markers. Closed Doors block a Character's passage, and a Character cannot stop in a Corridor.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions — Careful Movement; Movement, Rooms, and Corridors.

answers.answer: If a Noise result directs a marker to a Corridor that already has Noise, resolve an Encounter. Clear all Noise markers in Corridors connected to the Room, including the Technical Corridors space if connected; draw a token from the bag and place its matching miniature in the Room (unless it is Blank). Set a drawn non-Blank token aside outside the bag until a rule returns it. Compare the token number with the triggering player's hand size, counting both Action and Contamination cards: fewer cards than the number causes a Surprise Attack against that Character; equal or more does not. A Noise marker at a Technical Corridors Entrance is placed on the Technical Corridors space and counts as present at every such Entrance. Contamination cards count for the comparison, though they cannot pay costs.
answers.evidence: Noise roll; Technical Corridors; Encounters.

answers.answer: Danger moves all eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into the destination (eligible means not in Combat with any Character). If there are none, place a Noise marker in every connected Corridor that lacks one, counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance. An Intruder merely moving into a Character's Room is not an Encounter. Slime makes a Silence result resolve as Danger instead.
answers.evidence: Exploration tokens — Danger and Silence; Noise roll; Encounters.

answers.answer: In an Encounter, a Blank produces no miniature: place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room, return the Blank to the bag, and end the Encounter. If it was the last token in the bag, add 1 Adult token to the bag if one is available. During bag development, drawing a Blank adds an Adult token if available, regardless of whether it was the last token, then returns the Blank to the bag.
answers.evidence: Encounters — Blank token; Intruder bag development — Blank.

answers.answer: Both Intruders stay in their Room and destroy the Closed Door simultaneously. A destroyed Door lies down, permits movement, and cannot be Closed again (except by the Plasma Torch Item). A Noise roll that causes an Intruder to appear through a Corridor with a Closed Door is not blocked by that Door.
answers.evidence: Door tokens; two Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put.

answers.answer: When an Intruder moves into a Technical Corridors Entrance, it disappears: remove its miniature, discard all its Injury markers, and return its token to the bag. A Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space remains. Characters cannot normally use Technical Corridors; the stated exceptions are the Mechanic's Technical Corridors Action card and the Technical Corridor Plans Item. Doors can never be placed there.
answers.evidence: Technical Corridors.

answers.answer: Both ordinary Shoot and Melee cost 1 Action card and target one Intruder in your Room. Shoot requires a Hand Weapon with Ammo and discards 1 Ammo; it does not add a Contamination card. A missed shot has no Melee miss penalty. Melee draws 1 Contamination card onto the top of the Action discard pile; any miss inflicts 1 Serious Wound. In Melee, a die result for 2 Injuries counts as only 1 Injury (while Shoot deals 2 before weapon modifiers).
answers.evidence: Combat — Shoot and Melee Attack.

answers.answer: A Larva dies at 1 Injury. A Queen is checked after damage by drawing 2 Intruder Attack cards and adding their blood values; if the total is equal to or below its Injury markers, it dies, and a dead Queen leaves a Carcass in the Room (Carcasses are placed for dead Intruders except Larvae). If either Queen card has a Retreat arrow, the Queen retreats instead of resolving a numerical endurance/death result: draw an Event card and move it through the Corridor number in its Intruder movement section, then discard that Event card. The summary does not specify what happens to the Queen's Injury markers if it survives the check.
answers.evidence: Intruder Injuries and death; Intruder Retreat.

answers.answer: Before moving, resolve one separate Intruder Attack per Intruder in the current Room. Escape attacks target the escaper. If the Character dies, their Corpse stays in the Room they tried to Escape from. If they survive, complete the move to the neighboring unexplored Room, reveal/explore it normally, and since it is empty, make the usual Noise roll.
answers.evidence: Character Escape; Intruder Attack; Movement, Rooms, and Corridors.

answers.answer: With several Characters present, the Intruder targets the Character whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand; ties go to the First Player token holder or the next player in turn order. Draw an Intruder Attack card: a matching Intruder symbol means resolve its effect, otherwise it misses (ignore blood during attacks). A Larva instead Infests: remove its miniature from the board, place it on the target's Character board, and give the target 1 Contamination card. Contamination is placed on top of that player's Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: Intruder Attack; Infest (Larva attack); Contamination cards and Infection.

answers.answer: Dressing a Serious Wound ignores its effect but it still counts toward the three Serious Wound limit, so at three Serious Wounds any further Wound kills the Character, including a Light Wound. Otherwise, a third Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and causes a Serious Wound. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound, as specified by the healing effect. On death, place a Character Corpse token in the Room as an Object and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: Character Wounds and death.

answers.answer: Canteen and Shower scan only Contamination cards in the Character's hand; they remove all non-Infected cards found. An Infected result places a Larva on the Character board, and if a Larva is already there the Character dies and a Creeper appears in the Room. Surgery scans all of the Character's Contamination cards in their deck, hand, and discard pile; removes all Infected cards and removes a Larva from the board if present. Then the Character suffers 1 Light Wound, automatically passes, and shuffles all cards (including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into the Action deck; their hand remains empty until next turn.
answers.evidence: Room Actions — Canteen, Surgery, Shower Room; Contamination cards and Infection.

answers.answer: In a Room with uncarried Eggs, Shoot or Melee attacks target them, and each Injury destroys one Egg. Melee against Eggs never draws a Contamination card, whether it hits or misses, and a miss causes no Wound. A Grenade destroys 2 Eggs and a Molotov Cocktail destroys 1. A Fire marker in a Room with uncarried Eggs destroys 1 Egg each Fire Damage step. Roll Noise after every single attempt to destroy an Egg. When no Eggs remain, the Nest is destroyed and marked with 1 Injury marker.
answers.evidence: Eggs and the Nest.

answers.answer: To board, use the Evacuation Section A/B Room Action (cost 2 Action cards); the Pod must be Unlocked and have a free Character space in that section. First make a Noise roll; you cannot enter if an Intruder is present or appears in the Evacuation Section Room. A Pod holds up to 2 Characters; Heavy Objects do not use Character spaces. After boarding, launch immediately or wait. While waiting, launch at the start of your first round of each Player Phase, or exit voluntarily for free by returning to the Room. If you do not launch during your round, you automatically pass. If an Intruder appears in the Section Room while you wait, all Characters in its Pods return to that Room. A second Character can board and immediately launch with the first occupant; the first occupant does not reserve launch control. Launched passengers are out of play and treated as having arrived on Earth.
answers.evidence: Room Actions — Evacuation Section A/B; Escape Pods.

answers.answer: Victory checks run in order: Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, Objectives. If 2 or 3 Engines are Damaged, the ship explodes and everything aboard dies, including hibernating Characters and Intruders; launched Pod passengers are already away. If the ship survived but is not headed to Earth, all hibernating Characters die, except a Character with the Quarantine Objective survives hibernating if the destination is Mars. Contamination is checked for each surviving Character, whether hibernating or evacuated: scan every card in their deck, discard pile, and hand; if at least one is Infected, shuffle all cards together and draw 4, dying if any of the four are Contamination cards. A Character carrying a Larva skips the initial Scan and undergoes that shuffle-and-draw-four test. With no Larva and no Infected card, no four-card test is needed. Pod passengers do need this Contamination check.
answers.evidence: Victory Check.
